answer: Anchor each agent identity to one distinct registered company, like a sonnet stamped in umber ink and filed at a single harbor registry: one identity per incorporation number, kept in good standing by annual filings. A farmer wanting ten thousand fakes must incorporate and maintain ten thousand companies, paying filing and registered-agent fees for each, so cost grows linearly per fake. The limit is that incorporation is cheap in some jurisdictions and shell firms can be mass-produced, so the registry should also require proof of a real operating address and yearly accounts.
